overview.summary: Urban planners shape how towns and cities grow, planning where homes, workplaces, schools, parks, transport and services should go.
overview.problems: They balance housing, jobs, transport, the environment and the needs of different communities, now and in the future.
overview.worksWith: Local authorities, architects, engineers, developers, residents, and transport and environment specialists.
overview.workplaces: Local and regional government, planning consultancies, developers, universities and non-profits.

timeline.title: Review plans and proposals
timeline.description: The planner reads applications and development plans.
timeline.why: Each decision shapes how people live.

timeline.title: Site visits
timeline.description: The planner visits areas, checks conditions and takes notes and photos.
timeline.why: Seeing a place first-hand reveals what maps miss.

timeline.title: Analyzing data and maps
timeline.description: The planner uses maps, population and traffic data to test ideas.

timeline.title: Meeting people
timeline.description: The planner holds consultations with residents, businesses and officials.
timeline.why: Plans work better when communities help shape them.

timeline.title: Writing reports
timeline.description: The planner writes recommendations that follow laws and policies.
timeline.why: Decisions must be clear and justified.

timeline.title: Public meetings
timeline.description: Consultations are often held after work so that residents can attend.
timeline.why: Many people can only take part outside working hours.

responsibilities: Preparing and reviewing plans for land use and development
Analyzing data on population, traffic and the environment
challenges: Competing interests mean residents, developers and politicians often disagree.
Decisions can be slow, political and controversial.
Plans take years to show results.
Short-term needs always have to be balanced with long-term effects.
workEnvironment: Offices and meeting rooms, with regular site visits and public consultations. The work involves maps, data, documents and many discussions. Hours are usually regular but evening meetings are common.
rewards: A mix of analysis and creativity
tradeoffs: Pay and roles that vary by country and sector

activity.title: Audit your neighbourhood for walkability
steps: With an adult, walk a short route around your neighbourhood.
Note safe crossings, pavements, lighting, shade, seating and anything that makes walking hard.
Mark the problems on a simple sketch map.
Suggest three improvements and who would need to act on each.
Note whether looking at a place like a planner felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise observing a place, mapping problems and proposing improvements.
activity.safety: Walk with an adult, stay on safe public paths, do not photograph people, and do not enter private property.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
